#HeyDevelopers and #Product_Managers 

Looking to integrate seamless mobile payments into your app? ethio telecom’s telebirr API makes it easy, fast, and secure. Here’s how to get started with the telebirr payment gateway via https://lnkd.in/e2E72pBB

What is the telebirr API?
The telebirr API is a powerful mobile payment gateway provided by ethio telecom that allows developers and businesses to integrate digital wallet services into their applications. 
With telebirr, users can:
 ✅Make and receive payments
 ✅Access financial services securely and instantly
🛠️ How to Integrate Telebirr API: Step-by-Step Guide
1. Register on the Developer Portal
 Visit 👉🏻https://lnkd.in/eUEsvMbF
 Create an account and log in to access the API documentation and sandbox tools
2. Access the API Documentation
Navigate to the API Docs section https://lnkd.in/e2k6u9Bm for detailed integration guides and endpoints
3. Choose Your Integration Type
telebirr offers multiple integration options:
 B2B Integration – for businesses receiving payments
 Mini App Integration – for embedding services within the Telebirr SuperApp
4. Set Up Your Development Environment
 Use tools like #VS_Code and the Macle Developer Toolkit
 #Download demo projects to accelerate development
5. Configure API Keys and Endpoints
 Use the sandbox environment to test your integration
 Securely configure your API credentials, callback URLs, and transaction parameters
6. Test and Go Live
 Perform end-to-end testing in the sandbox
 Submit for approval and move to production once validated

🚀 Want to integrate fast, secure mobile payments into your app? Discover how to configure the telebirr API from Ethio telecom and start accepting payments in minutes. From sandbox testing to production-ready deployment, the developer portal https://lnkd.in/eUEsvMbF has everything you need to build with confidence. #Telebirr #APIIntegration #Fintech #EthioTelecom #MobilePayments #DeveloperTools

    🚀 Flutter App Performance Checklist Before Production (Lessons from Banking & Fintech Apps) Your Flutter app UI may look beautiful — but performance decides whether users stay or uninstall.     CleverTap has just released the BFSI Benchmark Report 2026 , consolidating key onboarding and conversion metrics across global banks and fintech companies. A few standout insights you may find useful: 1. Onboarding – the biggest drop-off point for growth 👉 The average web → signup conversion rate in BFSI is around 8.3%. Rates below this are often driven by long forms, complex UX, or unclear / overly technical language. 👉 On mobile apps, only ~21% of users who install the app complete signup within the first week — meaning nearly 80% drop off at the very first stage. 👉 70% of users who complete registration do so within the first 75 seconds. When onboarding takes more than 2 minutes, abandonment rates increase sharply. 2. Conversion – fast, but highly dependent on the first 7 days 👉 Around 95% of users who complete signup make at least one transaction within the first month, indicating very high intent in banking and fintech. 👉 76% of users complete their first transaction within ~7 days after signup. 👉 On average, users need only 2–5 app opens before converting. A higher number often signals friction or a lack of timely nudges during early lifecycle stages. Happy to share more BFSI insights — feel free to reach out 👏

    𝗙𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵’𝘀 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿 (𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝘽𝙡𝙞𝙣𝙙 𝙎𝙥𝙤𝙩) Fintech (rightly) loves to talk about Payments, KYC, Credit Scoring, and UX. Entire companies are built perfecting these layers. But there’s a 𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗽𝗼𝘁 we don’t talk about enough.  𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗶𝘁𝘆. Most Fintech are built on 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.  𝘜𝘴𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘢𝘭𝘸𝘢𝘺𝘴 𝘰𝘯𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘦. That assumption breaks more often than we think. Especially for: 𝘊𝘳𝘰𝘴𝘴 𝘣𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘶𝘴𝘦𝘳𝘴.  𝘔𝘰𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘧𝘪𝘳𝘴𝘵 𝘶𝘴𝘦𝘳𝘴. 𝘞𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘵𝘺 𝘥𝘳𝘰𝘱𝘴, 𝘴𝘰 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴 𝘗𝘢𝘺𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘴. I saw this up close recently. My daughter recently relocated for Uni.  Her first visit home. No access to payments. Why? 𝘕𝘰 𝘮𝘰𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘵𝘺. Extended family visited from Australia.  Those without connectivity meant no payment options. Apps open. Payments don’t go through. Why?  𝘕𝘰 𝘥𝘢𝘵𝘢. 𝘕𝘰 𝘊𝘰𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘵𝘺. We call these ‘𝘦𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘤𝘢𝘴𝘦𝘴’.  For many users 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲. This isn’t just a “𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺.”  It is a 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗲. Because the user doesn’t care which layer failed. They 𝘦𝘹𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘯𝘤𝘦 𝘵𝘳𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘣𝘳𝘰𝘬𝘦𝘯 at the point of payment. Fintech optimizes everything inside an app. But the very 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘥𝘦𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘤𝘺 '𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗶𝘁𝘆', is 𝘭𝘦𝘧𝘵 𝘵𝘰 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦. 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗽𝗼𝘁. Connectivity shouldn’t be an afterthought. It 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗯𝗲 𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗱𝗲𝗱. That is what we are building at Firsty.app #Telecom #Fintech #Payments #Connectivity #Mobile #Digital #Apps

    Building a New Mobile App in 2026? Here's What You Need to Know About Architecture Whether you're starting with Android Compose or going cross-platform with KMP, choosing the right architecture matters. But here's what most developers get wrong: they think it's an either/or decision between MVVM, Clean Architecture, and Multi-Module. The truth? You need all three working together, but when and how you apply them depends on what you're building. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗠𝗩𝗩𝗠 + 𝗖𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 Every modern Android app should start here. MVVM separates UI from business logic. Clean Architecture organizes code into three layers: presentation, domain, and data. This combination works for any app size. 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝗔𝗱𝗱 𝗠𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶-𝗠𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗹𝗲 Here's my rule: modularize when complexity demands it, not because it's trendy. You need multi-module architecture when: • Your team has 3-4+ developers working simultaneously • Build times exceed 2-3 minutes • You have distinct features that can be developed independently • You're building banking, fintech, or e-commerce apps Banking apps are perfect examples. You might have feature modules for accounts, transfers, cards, loans, and investments. Each module works independently. The accounts team doesn't block the transfers team. Don't modularize a simple MVP. The overhead isn't worth it until your codebase reaches that complexity. 𝗦𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗲 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 𝘃𝘀 𝗖𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀-𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 For Android-only: Start with MVVM + Clean Architecture. Add multi-module when complexity justifies it. For cross-platform with KMP: Same architecture principles, different structure. Share 60-90% of your code between Android and iOS, including business logic, data layer, and ViewModels. Platform-specific code handles UI and system integrations. 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗕𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗳𝗶𝘁𝘀 • New developers onboard 40-50% faster • KMP reduces code duplication by 60-90% • Multi-module cuts build times by 30-50% • Fewer merge conflicts with separate modules • Better testing with well-defined boundaries 𝗠𝘆 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲 Start simple. Use MVVM + Clean Architecture from day one. Add multi-module when your team grows beyond 3-4 developers, build times become frustrating, or you're building complex apps like banking and fintech. Consider KMP when you need both platforms and want to share business logic while maintaining native performance. Don't modularize for the sake of it. Don't go cross-platform if you only need one platform. Make decisions based on actual needs, not trends. The goal is shipping great apps efficiently. Architecture is the tool that gets you there. What architecture are you using? I'd love to hear what's working for you. #AndroidDev #KMP #ComposeMultiplatform #CleanArchitecture #MVVM #Kotlin #iOSDev #MobileArchitecture
